alerts-bot: [SEV3] KV-cache hit_rate anomaly - eu-central replica set. start=2026-03-13T07:30:00Z. hit_rate=22% (expected > 90%). auto-paging to on-call. alert_id=KV_HIT_EUC_1774609800 :loud_sound:
oncall-lee: Acking. I'm on it. Not seeing any scheduled deploys in the last 4h. @infra-bot any autoscaler events or machine restarts?
infra-bot: No cluster node restarts. Autoscaler did a brief dry-run 2h ago, but no new nodes were created. No config pushes detected.
mira: I'm seeing a correlated spike in keyspace_keys (unique keys) for the cache namespace: +1.1M keys over 20m on shard eu-kv-02. TTL average dropped from 48h to 3s for a subset of keys (likely TTL bug in ingestion).
alex: If TTLs dropped to seconds that would create churn and evictions. Are evictions spiking too?
mira: Yes - evicted_keys increased ~4200 in 10m on eu-kv-02. Memory used ~9.4G / maxmemory 10G. RSS trending up.
oncall-lee: Oof. Customer impact: I'm seeing retried backend calls from the text-generation proxy and a 20% increase in 429s for some high-QPS tenants. Posting a short status to customers with mitigation steps.
paul: Can you dump the slowlog or a sample of keys to check prefixes? Might be a tenant generating many high-cardinality keys.
mira: Pasting sample key list (redacted):
```
cache:user:abcd1234:session:xyz
cache:user:abcd1234:ctx:2026-03-13T07:28:11
cache:tenant:big-co:message:0000001
cache:temp:run:uuid-5990
```
Looks like a mix of long-lived and ephemeral keys; suspect ingestion TTL defaulting bug.
oncall-lee: Short-term mitigation plan: 1) throttle writes to the cache ingestion topic for suspected tenant(s), 2) increase maxmemory on eu-kv-02 by 25%, 3) spin up an extra replica for the shard. Doing 2 & 3 now.
oncall-lee: `kubectl -n infra scale statefulset eu-kv --replicas=4`
infra-bot: Replica scale initiated. New pod ready in ~40s.
oncall-lee: Patching env on eu-kv-02 to bump MAX_MEMORY=12g: `kubectl -n infra set env statefulset/eu-kv MAX_MEMORY=12g`
mira: After scale + mem bump: evictions/sec back down, hit_rate climbing to ~86% over 6m. Proxy latencies improving.
alex: Nice. I'm going to trigger a temporary inbound write throttle for namespace `cache:tenant:big-co` to stop the hammering and give us time to triage.
paul: Made a note - need to collect per-tenant miss ratio and churn (new_keys/min) for the post-incident.
oncall-lee: Opening an incident ticket INC-3461 and will mark mitigated once metrics are stable.
oncall-lee: INC-3461: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-3461  initial impact: elevated latency and errors for some tenants in eu-central due to cache churn. Mitigation: scale & mem bump + write throttle.
mira: For follow-up, propose we: (A) add eviction spike pager routed to infra team, (B) make hit_rate alerts less noisy by correlating with eviction_rate and p99 latency, (C) surface per-tenant unique keys in Grafana.
alex: I second correlating signals. Current pager triggers only on global hit_rate. That floods with noise during deployments or cache-clears. Suggested rules:
- SEV3 page if per-shard evicted_keys_sum over 5m > 1000 AND hit_rate < 70%
- SEV2 if evicted_keys_sum over 1m > 3000 (rapid storm)
- Warning (no page) if hit_rate < 65% for 10m AND p99_latency < 450ms
- Page if per-tenant new_keys/min > 5000 sustained 5m (hot-tenant)
paul: Also adding: alert when avg TTL < 60s for > 2m on a shard (indicates ingestion TTL bug).
oncall-lee: Good call. We should also add an automated short-circuit: if eviction storm detected (>3000/min), auto-scale +1 replica and send a runbook link to the oncall. Limit auto-run once per hour to avoid flip-flop.
mira: I'll own MON-790 to build the Grafana dashboard cards: per-shard hit_rate, evictions/sec, mem RSS vs maxmemory, per-tenant new_keys/min, per-tenant miss_ratio, TTL distribution heatmap.
alex: RUNBOOK updates: RUNBOOK-13  document how to identify TTL regressions, throttle writes, scale shards, bump memory, and how to audit tenant key cardinality. I'll pick it up.
oncall-lee: For immediate customer comms I'll post a short note: "Transient cache pressure in eu-central caused increased misses and throttling for some customers; we've scaled the cache and mitigated. We will follow up with root cause and prevention steps."
infra-bot: Monitoring: no eviction spikes in last 25m, per-shard hit_rate stabilizing ~89%.
paul: A few follow-ups: implement per-tenant quota on unique keys, TTL-linting in CI for ingestion services, and a nightly TTL hygiene job to evict tiny TTLs created by bugs.
mira: Scheduling 45m postmortem tomorrow 14:00 UTC to review metrics and agree on which alerts to ship. Invite channel: #oncall-postmortems.
oncall-lee: Handing off to mira for post-incident ownership. Action items:
- MON-790 (owner: mira) dashboard work
- ALERT-433 (owner: alex) alert rule changes + pager tuning
- RUNBOOK-13 (owner: alex) runbook updates
- INC-3461 (owner: oncall-lee) incident writeup and customer notes
alex: Quick note: implement an ops endpoint to list per-tenant keycardinality and top prefixes; will help debug fast.
oncall-lee: I'm marking incident mitigated and closing the pager. If anyone sees reoccurrence re-open INC-3461. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
alerts-bot: Incident marked mitigated. Reminder: please file follow-ups within 72h.
mira: I'll attach graphs and the sample key dumps to the incident. Closing thread. :thumbsup:
